regions.region: page 1 title, author block, abstract, and article metadata
regions.finding: Verified the source-derived title, article identity, and aggregate [6+2] annulation claim. No SI association was inferred from the article's later availability statement.
Examples of benzazocine-containing natural products and a receptor ligand; no reaction arrows or current-paper experimental conditions occur in this panel.
Generic, explicitly well-established transition-metal reactions of alpha-leaving-group allenes are classified as cited literature examples, not current-paper experiments.

Scheme 1c is a proposed unsaturated-bond insertion concept with Int-A/Int-B; Scheme 1d is the generic current annulation and depicts non-formation of the six-membered alternative. Experiment-specific rows are recorded from Table 1/Schemes 2–5.

The 1a/2a model reaction discussion maps to Table 1 entries 1–7. Entries 1–4 give zero product, entry 5 gives 30% (Z)-3aa with 3aa' not observed, and L5/L6 screening continues on page 2; no duplicate prose-only records were created.

unresolved: Scheme 1 generic structures do not define unique molecules or experiment-specific yields.

regions.region: page 2 upper-left Table 1 header, entries 1–15, ligand drawings, and footnotes
regions.finding: Fifteen independent optimization rows were retained with 1a scale, 2a equivalents, Pd2(dba)3/ligand loadings including footnote overrides, base identity/2 equiv, toluene/r.t./24 h, NMR yields, recovery, CH3NO2 basis, and entry-15 80% isolated yield. Entry 15 is merged with ordinary Scheme 3 (Z)-3aa rather than duplicated.

Four distinct N-protecting-group experiments (1b–1e) were retained. Desired products are not formed and substrate recoveries 82/61/85/26% are separately targeted to the corresponding starting materials.
Narrative scope statements map to the 19 ordinary Scheme 3 products on page 3. The 4 mmol/1.3872 g/78% 3aa experiment is a separate scale-up from the ordinary 0.5 mmol/80% experiment.

The text reports the PTAD reactions to products 4 and 5 and qualitative excellent diastereoselectivity for 5; Scheme 4 on page 3 supplies the arrow conditions and the third product-4-to-6 transformation.
The no-terminal-allene control is linked to Scheme 5 equation 1 on page 3; it remains one cross-page failed experiment.

unresolved: Most main-text scope rows omit solvent volume, atmosphere, workup, purification, and product mass.
Scheme 4 gives no numeric diastereomeric ratio for product 5.

regions.region: page 3 upper Scheme 3 shared arrow and nineteen product structures
regions.finding: Nineteen ordinary scope products were inventoried row by row under 1 (0.5 mmol), 2 (1.5 equiv), Pd2(dba)3 5 mol%, L6 17.5 mol%, Cs2CO3 2 equiv, toluene, room temperature, 24 h. Ordinary 3aa is merged with Table 1 entry 15; the other 18 remain independent rows.

regions.region: page 3 Scheme 3 footnote and 3aa scale-up annotation
regions.finding: The 4 mmol 1a/1.5 equiv 2a/20 mL toluene run gives (Z)-3aa in 78% (1.3872 g) and is retained as a separate scale-up.

Three independent arrows were retained: (Z)-3ag + 1.5 equiv PTAD at room temperature/8 h to 4 (59%); (Z)-3ag + 3 equiv PTAD at 120 °C/8 h to 5 (51%); and 4 + 3 equiv diethyl acetylenedicarboxylate at 120 °C/8 h to 6 (55%). ORTEP of 5 is characterization only.

Three independent controls were retained: omission of allene, replacement by styrene, and replacement by diphenylacetylene. Crossed expected products are non-detections; 1a recoveries are 27%, 38%, and 34%.

regions.region: page 3 lower text and beginning of Scheme 6 discussion
regions.finding: Control interpretation and the proposed Pd0/L(allene) catalytic cycle are linked to their Scheme 5/6 records rather than duplicated as prose experiments.

unresolved: Complex scope structures and intermediates remain label-only where safe encoding was not possible.
Recovery measurement basis/detection limits are not printed for Scheme 5.

regions.region: page 4 upper-left Scheme 6 and mechanism continuation
regions.finding: Species I and intermediates II–V form a plausible catalytic cycle; they are proposed, not isolated preparations. The crossed E-product path is retained as a mechanistic nonfavored branch.
Conclusions summarize the annulation, control experiments, and inability of alkene/alkyne replacements to react; no new experiment, condition, or yield is introduced.

Huanan Wang is thanked for reproducing (Z)-3ab, (Z)-3an, and (Z)-3ga. Because no independent charges, conditions, yields, or run identifiers are given, these are provenance notes on existing Scheme 3 rows and do not create duplicate experiments.
